title: trustdiff baseline, schema version 1
description: The record a project keeps of the trust signals it has observed for the packages it locks, written to .trustdiff/baseline.json by trustdiff baseline and by diff and scan with --update-baseline. It exists because a registry answers about now: PyPI records no publisher per version and crates.io keeps no maintainer history, so a project that wants to be told when either changed has to remember what it saw. One shape serves every ecosystem. Within schema version 1 fields are added, never renamed or removed; a breaking change bumps the version in the schema field and in this file's name.

schema.description: Identifies the document format. Always trustdiff.baseline/1 for documents that match this schema.

updated_at.description: When the file was last written, in RFC 3339 with second precision in UTC. It is the run's clock, not the wall clock of the file system, and an entry whose signals a rerun found unchanged keeps the observed_at it already carried, so a rewrite that observed nothing new produces no diff beyond this line.

packages.description: One entry per package, sorted by ecosystem and then by name, so a rewrite produces the smallest possible diff and a repository does not churn. A package appears at most once, whatever the number of lockfiles that lock it.

package.description: The trust signals observed for one package at one moment: who maintained it, who published the release that was looked at, and what provenance that release carried.

ecosystem.description: Registry the package lives in. deno and jsr are accepted from milestone M4 on.

name.description: Package name in the registry's canonical spelling: PEP 503 normalized for pypi, unchanged elsewhere. Scoped npm and jsr names keep their @scope/ prefix. A baseline records what the lockfile or the command line spelled, which for cargo can differ from the spelling a report carries, because a run adopts the registry's own.

version.description: The release the observation was taken from, which is the version the project locked when the entry was written. A package locked at several versions in one project is recorded once, at the first version in ref order, and the run says so.

observed_at.description: When the signals below were first seen at the registry, in RFC 3339 with second precision in UTC. A rerun that reads the same signals leaves it alone, so that a project which observed nothing new rewrites no entry; the document's updated_at says when the record was last confirmed. A finding built on this entry states its age, because an old record still answers but says less about when a change happened. A signal a run could not read keeps the value recorded before rather than being erased, so an entry may hold signals read at different times, with observed_at naming the oldest of them.

maintainers.description: The maintainer or owner set the registry showed at observed_at, sorted and without repeats: npm maintainers, PyPI roles and organization, crates.io owners including teams. Absent when the set could not be read, which is not the same as a package with no maintainers: a check that finds it absent reports itself as skipped rather than reading it as an empty set.

items.description: One maintainer, owner or team as the registry names it, for example alice, org:pypa or github:rust-lang:libs.

publisher.description: The identity that published the release named in version. Absent when the registry exposes none and the release carries no attestation either. publisher_source says which of the two it is, and a check compares only identities from the same source.

publisher_source.description: Where the publisher value came from: registry for an account the registry itself recorded (npm _npmUser, crates.io published_by), provenance for the identity of the release's attestation or trusted publisher, which is the only publishing identity PyPI exposes. Present whenever publisher is.

provenance.description: The publishing evidence the observed release carried. Absent when the registry could not be asked, so that a later run does not read a failed lookup as evidence that the release had none.

kind.description: The strongest kind of evidence the release carried: none, signature for a registry signature, attestation for a build attestation (npm provenance, PEP 740, SLSA), trusted-publisher for a trusted publishing identity the registry recorded.

verified.description: True when the registry or deps.dev verified the evidence rather than only carrying it.

identity.description: The workflow or repository the evidence names, for example github:pypa/sampleproject/release.yml. Absent when the evidence names none.
